pointers.sentence: The decorators of `django/views/decorators/`, such as `require_http_methods`, `never_cache` and `csrf_exempt`: the wrappers they put around a view, acting before the call or after it, the marks some leave for other code to read, and how `condition` answers a request without calling the view.

Each decorator whose wrapper is written in `django/views/decorators/`, all but `sensitive_variables`, defines that wrapper twice, once with `def` and once with `async def`, picks one by asking whether the view is a coroutine function, and passes it through `functools.wraps` (`django/views/decorators/cache.py:never_cache`).

Each decorator whose wrapper is written in `django/views/decorators/`, all but `sensitive_variables`, defines that wrapper twice, once with `def` and once with `async def`, picks one by asking whether the view is a coroutine function, and passes it through `functools.wraps` (`django/views/decorators/cache.py:never_cache`).

The decorators made from a middleware class are defined in the directory too, but get their two wrappers from `make_middleware_decorator`, which is written to the same pattern (`django/utils/decorators.py:make_middleware_decorator`).
The ones Django supplies ready-made, such as `require_GET` and `vary_on_cookie`, are the result of such a call kept under a name (`django/views/decorators/http.py:require_GET`).

The wrapper that `require_http_methods` makes compares the request's method with its list, and if the method is not there it returns an `HttpResponseNotAllowed` naming the list, logs a warning, and never calls what it wraps (`django/views/decorators/http.py:require_http_methods`).

The docstring asks for the methods in upper case, and nothing converts the list (`django/views/decorators/http.py:require_http_methods`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.__init__`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).

Written under `condition`, `vary_on_cookie` runs only when the view does; written over it, it patches the 304 as well ([Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](../services/http-caching.md#under-the-condition-decorator)) (`django/views/decorators/http.py:condition`).

*The view decorators of `django/views/decorators/` that are not made from a middleware, by when each changes the request or the response.
If the client already holds the current version and the request is a `"GET"` or a `"HEAD"`, the answer is a 304 and the view is never called (`django/views/decorators/http.py:condition`).

How `get_conditional_response` compares the versions, the 412 it gives a request that would replace a version other than the current one, and how the wrapper quotes a tag and reads a time without a time zone, are told in [Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](../services/http-caching.md), with `ConditionalGetMiddleware`, which makes the same decision for a `"GET"` from the finished response, and so only after the view has done its work.

`csrf_exempt` and `no_append_slash` return a wrapper that does nothing but call the view, and set an attribute on the wrapper, `"csrf_exempt"` or `"should_append_slash"` (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:csrf_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/common.py:no_append_slash`).

`csrf_exempt` and `no_append_slash` return a wrapper that does nothing but call the view, and set an attribute on the wrapper, `"csrf_exempt"` or `"should_append_slash"` (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:csrf_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/common.py:no_append_slash`).

`non_atomic_requests`, in `django/db/transaction.py`, marks its wrapper in the same way, with `"_non_atomic_requests"`, a set of database aliases, which a second use of the decorator copies with its own added (`django/db/transaction.py:_non_atomic_requests`).

Setting the attribute on the view itself would work as well, and the comment at the head of `csrf_exempt` and of `no_append_slash` says so; each returns a new function because, in that comment's words, "decorators are nicer if they don't have side effects" (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:csrf_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/common.py:no_append_slash`).

`login_not_required`, in `django/contrib/auth/decorators.py`, takes the other course: it sets its attribute on the view it is given and returns that same view (`django/contrib/auth/decorators.py:login_not_required`).

`"should_append_slash"` is read by `CommonMiddleware.should_redirect_with_slash`, which resolves the path with a slash added to find the view it would lead to, and is called from that middleware's `process_request` and `process_response` ([What the handler asks of a view](callable.md#what-other-code-reads-from-a-view)) (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.should_redirect_with_slash`).

`csp_override` and `csp_report_only_override` each store a policy on the response, which `ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_response` uses in place of the one in the settings (`django/views/decorators/clickjacking.py:xframe_options_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/csp.py:_make_csp_decorator`).

`sensitive_post_parameters` sets an attribute of its own name on the request each time the view is called, holding the names of the posted fields that an error report must not show, `("password",)` for `sensitive_post_parameters("password")`, or `"__ALL__"` for `sensitive_post_parameters()` (`django/views/decorators/debug.py:sensitive_post_parameters`).
